electoral_votes_2028.source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census Apportionment Table 1 (House seats) + 2 senators; DC = 3 (23rd Amendment). The 2020-census apportionment governs the 2024 and 2028 elections; next reapportionment follows the 2030 census (first used in 2032). Mid-decade House redistricting does not change electoral votes.
electoral_votes_2028.definition: Electors for the 2028 election. Maine/Nebraska state rows carry only the 2 at-large electors; each district row carries 1 (electoral_votes_state_total_2028 gives the state total). Sum across rows = 538.

pres2024.source: Wikipedia, 2024 United States presidential election, Results by state table (certified state canvasses cited per row)
pres2024.definition: dem_votes/rep_votes/total_votes as certified; dem_pct and rep_pct = share of all presidential votes cast (incl. third parties); margin = dem_pct - rep_pct in percentage points (positive = Democratic lead). ME/NE district rows from the same table.

pres2020_margin.source: Wikipedia, 2020 United States presidential election, Results by state table
pres2020_margin.definition: (Biden - Trump) / total votes, percentage points, positive = Democratic. District rows on 2012-2021 lines.

pres2016_margin.source: Wikipedia, 2016 United States presidential election, Results by state table
pres2016_margin.definition: (Clinton - Trump) / total votes, percentage points, positive = Democratic. District rows on 2012-2021 lines.

pres2020_margin_current_lines_rounded.source: Wikipedia district pages, 'Recent election results from statewide races' tables (citing Dave's Redistricting App)
pres2020_margin_current_lines_rounded.definition: Dem minus Rep, whole percentage points, computed from the rounded percentages shown (e.g. Biden 52% - 46% -> 6). District rows only. Same for pres2016_margin_current_lines_rounded.

turnout_2024_vep.source: University of Florida Election Lab (Michael McDonald), 2024 General Election Turnout v0.4 (3/2/2026)
turnout_2024_vep.definition: Total ballots counted / voting-eligible population, percent. Flag turnout_2024_ballots_is_rounded_estimate = true where UF lists a round-number ballot total (AL, MS, MO, OK, PA, TN, TX), i.e. highest-office votes plus an estimate rather than reported total ballots. Not available for districts.

race_ethnicity (white_nh_pct_cvap, black.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Citizen Voting Age Population by Race and Ethnicity special tabulation, 2020-2024 5-year ACS (State.csv, CD.csv for 119th Congress districts)
race_ethnicity (white_nh_pct_cvap, black.definition: Share of citizens 18+. White/Black/Asian = non-Hispanic single race alone; Hispanic of any race; other = remainder (non-Hispanic AIAN, NHPI, and all multiracial combinations). Shares sum to 100.

white_noncollege_pct_adults25 / white_co.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year, table C15002H (White alone, not Hispanic, 25+, by educational attainment) divided by B15003_001 (all persons 25+)
white_noncollege_pct_adults25 / white_co.definition: Non-Hispanic white adults 25+ without / with a bachelor's degree, as % of ALL residents 25+ (not citizens-only; ACS has no race x education x citizenship table). District rows use 119th-Congress district geography.

bachelors_plus_pct_cvap.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year, table B29002 (CVAP by educational attainment)
bachelors_plus_pct_cvap.definition: Citizens 18+ with a bachelor's or graduate/professional degree, % of CVAP (all races).

age_18_29_pct_cvap / age_65plus_pct_cvap.source: Census ACS 2024 1-year, table B29001 (CVAP by age)
age_18_29_pct_cvap / age_65plus_pct_cvap.definition: Citizens aged 18-29 and 65+ as % of citizens 18+. cvap_acs1_2024 = B29001_001E.

median_household_income.definition: Median household income in the past 12 months, 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars.

urban_pct_2020_census.source: 2020 Census Demographic and Housing Characteristics (DHC) table P2 (Urban and Rural) for states; Wikipedia district infoboxes for ME/NE districts
urban_pct_2020_census.definition: Population living in Census-defined 2020 urban areas, % of total population. The Census urban/rural split has no suburban category; use urbanization_index_538 as a continuous density measure.

urbanization_index_538.source: FiveThirtyEight urbanization index (data repo, built from 2017 5-year ACS tract populations)
urbanization_index_538.definition: Natural log of the average number of people living within a 5-mile radius of each resident in the state (higher = more urban/suburban; ~8.7 AK to ~13.4 DC). States only.

white_evangelical_pct_adults_prri2025.source: PRRI American Values Atlas 2025 (data behind the 2025 PRRI Census of American Religion), Religious Affiliation by state
white_evangelical_pct_adults_prri2025.definition: White evangelical Protestants as % of adults, whole percentages as published. National = 13%. States only.

union_member_pct_2025.source: BLS, Union Members news release, Table 5: Union affiliation of employed wage and salary workers by state, 2024-2025 annual averages (released Jan 2026)
union_member_pct_2025.definition: Members of unions as % of employed wage and salary workers. 2025 values are 11-month averages (October 2025 not collected due to the federal shutdown). union_member_pct_2024 from the same table. States only.

independent_share.definition: Left null: no consistent 50-state source. About 20 states have no party registration, and registration-based "unaffiliated" shares are not comparable to self-identified independents; Gallup has not published state-level party ID in recent years.

rows.name: New York
rows.verification_note: pres2016_margin 22.49 (Wikipedia, all fusion lines) vs 22.32 computed from UCSB American Presidency Project (Clinton 4,491,191 / Trump 2,790,073 / total 7,622,328), which appears to count fewer party lines. Could not reach NY BOE (403) for a third source; value kept.

rows.name: Washington
rows.verification_note: pres2016_margin 15.71 uses a denominator that includes write-ins (3,317,019 per Wikipedia). WA Secretary of State official page (https://results.vote.wa.gov/results/20161108/President-Vice-President.html) shows the same Clinton 1,742,718 / Trump 1,221,747 but total 3,209,214 'not including write-ins', giving 16.23. Value kept; definitional, not an error.

notes: Base table for 2028 simulation: 51 state/DC rows + 5 district rows (ME-1, ME-2, NE-1, NE-2, NE-3) = 56 rows; electoral votes sum to 538 (ME and NE state rows hold only their 2 at-large electors). All margins are Dem minus Rep as % of total votes (positive = D). No 2026 midterm results are in this file; it is pre-election baseline data. Demographic shares mix universes, each labelled in the column name: _cvap = citizens 18+, _adults25 = all residents 25+, _adults = all adults (PRRI survey). CVAP race shares are 2020-2024 5-year ACS; age, education, income are 2024 1-year ACS (district values have larger sampling error). Values were computed in python from downloaded Census/UF/538 files; BLS Table 5 and PRRI AVA values were transcribed from the rendered pages (BLS cross-checked twice and against members/employed counts). turnout_2024_vep uses UF Election Lab v0.4 (provisional version label; 7 states use round-number ballot estimates).

verification.method: Electoral votes checked against 2020 apportionment (51 states + DC, ME/NE split 2 at-large + 1 per district; sum 538). Presidential dem/rep votes and margins for 2024, 2020 and 2016 recomputed for all 51 state/DC rows and NE-1..3 (all years) and ME-1/ME-2 (2024, 2020) from an independent source: UCSB American Presidency Project (https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/elections/2024, /2020, /2016). Demographics spot-checked for 10 states (AZ, CA, GA, MI, NV, NC, OH, PA, TX, WI) against Census Reporter's mirror of ACS 2024 1-year (https://api.censusreporter.org/1.0/data/show/acs2024_1yr?table_ids=B19013,B29001,B29002,C15002H,B15003): median income, CVAP total, age 18-29/65+, bachelor's+, white college/non-college shares; union rates for 13 states against BLS Table 5; VEP turnout for 11 states against the UF Election Lab v0.4 CSV. Margins sign convention (D minus R) confirmed on every row; dem_pct/rep_pct internally consistent with votes/total on every row.
unresolved: 2024 total_votes differ from UCSB for 14 rows (DE, GA, ID, ME, ME-1, ME-2, MT, NE, NE-1, NE-2, NE-3, PA, WV, WI): candidate votes identical, file totals include write-ins/other votes; resulting margin differences <= 0.2 pp (largest NE-3 -53.60 vs -53.80). Kept as definitional.

Historic margin denominators differ from UCSB by >0.05 pp in: NE 2020 (-19.06 vs -19.15), DE 2016 (11.37 vs 11.43), MT 2016 (-20.42 vs -20.53), WV 2016 (-42.07 vs -42.15), NY 2016 (22.49 vs 22.32), WA 2016 (15.71 vs 16.23; WA SOS official total excludes write-ins). Kept; see row notes for NY and WA.
ME-1/ME-2 pres2016_margin not independently confirmed (not in UCSB table; web search budget exhausted).

CVAP 5-year race/ethnicity shares, urban_pct_2020_census, urbanization_index_538 and PRRI evangelical shares not independently re-checked: Census API now requires a key and search budget was exhausted. Race shares sum to 100 +/-0.01 on spot-checked rows.
